diagnostic_attempts.cause: orchestration race in the lane bootstrap: in both lane sandboxes scripts/bootstrap_ci_environment.py --execute stopped at its last step 'typed service health' (exit 1) after every earlier step passed, before any test was collected or run; the Compose healthcheck of the Temporal server is only a TCP check of port 7233, so the stack is declared up while the Temporal frontend is still starting, and the single typed probe of deploy/bootstrap/services/temporal/qualify.py (no wait) ran too early. Three non-qualifying diagnostic reproductions with the harness functions (one lane sandbox, same head, same tools; ~/.ocor-codex/rem-0054-q/diag/diag_lane.py) show the same stop and the cause: typed status of temporal DEGRADED 'Temporal cluster health is not SERVING' (run 1) and 'describing an absent Temporal namespace did not fail closed' (run 2), with every other service READY; in run 3 the Temporal container started at 11:38:03.07Z, the probe failed at 11:38:40.6Z (not SERVING) and 11:38:49.9Z (namespace not failing closed) and passed at 11:39:02.2Z, about 59 s after the start, while the bootstrap typed check runs about 30-35 s after it

same orchestration race as attempt a1-two-lane-temporal-startup-race: both lane bootstraps stopped at 'typed service health' (exit 1) before any test. Diagnostic reproduction 4 (non-qualifying, one lane sandbox): the Temporal server container started at 11:46:04.32Z and logged its service start within one second, then logged nothing for 48.4 s (11:46:05.47Z to 11:46:53.84Z, first activity poll); the probe failed at 11:46:36.6Z (cluster health not SERVING, each CLI call reaching its 5 s command timeout) and passed at 11:47:01.3Z, about 57 s after the start; the bootstrap typed check runs about 30-35 s after the start, once
